beats.text: Two kings. One crown. Napoleon took it.
Spain, 1808. A weak king, Charles the Fourth. And a hated favourite who really ran the country: Manuel Godoy.
beats.say: Spain, eighteen-oh-eight. A weak king, Charles the Fourth. And a hated favourite who really ran the country: Manuel Godoy.

beats.text: Godoy let French troops march through Spain to attack Portugal. Soon they were everywhere.
In March, a mob stormed Godoy's palace. Two days later, the king gave up the crown to his own son, Ferdinand.
Napoleon invited father and son to Bayonne, in France, to settle their quarrel. It was a trap.
In Madrid, the French moved to take away the last of the royal family. The crowd exploded. Knives and stones against cavalry.
That night, the French shot the prisoners they had taken.
Goya painted it six years later. A man in a white shirt, arms wide open, facing the guns.
Days later in Bayonne, both kings signed the crown away. Napoleon gave Spain to his brother, Joseph.
He thought Spain was finished. Instead, the whole country rose.

beats.sub: Follow so you don't miss it
